question: Across the main conformal prediction methods designed for distribution shift (weighted conformal prediction for covariate shift, label-shift-adapted conformal prediction, adaptive/online conformal methods for temporal drift, and non-exchangeable conformal prediction with weighted or drift-discounted calibration), which finite-sample or asymptotic coverage guarantees does each retain, and what specific assumptions (e.g., known or estimable density ratios, label-conditional shift invariance, bounded total-variation drift, or adversarial-sequence regret-style guarantees) does each require for that guarantee to hold?
why_researchable: The literature is well developed and the core papers state their theorems and assumptions explicitly (Tibshirani et al. 2019 on weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift, Podkopaev & Ramdas 2021 on label shift, Gibbs & Candès 2021 on adaptive conformal inference, Barber et al. 2023 on non-exchangeable conformal prediction, and Gibbs & Candès 2022 and Zaffran et al. 2022 on time-series adaptivity). A short review can extract and compare the guarantee type (marginal vs conditional, exact vs approximate, long-run vs finite-sample), the required assumptions, and the failure modes in a structured table. No experiments are needed, so it fits a format-paper literature review.
no_parent_reason: This is a literature review question answered by synthesizing published theorems and assumptions, so no parent method or experiment is needed.
